The '''Qarachil Expedition''', also known as the '''[[Kumaon Kingdom|Kumaon]] Expedition''',<ref name="disha publication">{{cite book |last1=Experts |first1=Disha |title=The History Compendium for IAS Prelims General Studies CSAT Paper 1, UPSC & State PSC 2nd Edition |date=11 July 2017 |publisher=Disha Publications |isbn=978-93-86323-44-6 |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/The_History_Compendium_for_IAS_Prelims_G/OLctDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&pg=PA193&printsec=frontcover |language=en}}</ref><ref name="kumaon">{{cite book |last1=Ḥusain |first1=Āg̲h̲ā Mahdī |title=Tughluq Dynasty |date=1963 |publisher=Thacker, Spink |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Tughluq_Dynasty/XGA9AAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=qarachil+expedition&dq=qarachil+expedition&printsec=frontcover |language=en}}</ref><ref name="garhkumaon"/><ref name="Kumaon Garhwal"/> was a [[military campaign]] undertaken by Sultan [[Muhammad bin Tughluq]] of the [[Delhi Sultanate]] during the 14th century at 1337-38CE{{refn|group=note|Date of the Qarachil Expedition according to historians:
Budauni: fixes the expedition in 1337–1338 CE (738 Hijri); Firishta: also supports the date 1337–1338 CE (738 Hijri).
Some earlier assumptions placed the expedition as late as 1338 CE, but this is corrected by both Budauni and Firishta<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ḥusain |first1=Āg̲h̲ā Mahdī |title=Tughluq Dynasty |date=1963 |publisher=Thacker, Spink |pages=490 |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Tughluq_Dynasty/XGA9AAAAMAAJ?hl=en |language=en}}</ref>}}. The campaign aimed to secure the northern frontiers.
Qarachil is also referred to as Kumaon.<ref name="garhkumaon"/><ref name="kumaon"/><ref name="journal">{{cite book |title=Central Asiatic Journal |date=1975 |publisher=O. Harrassowitz |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Central_Asiatic_Journal/m_o-AQAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=0&bsq=qarachil%20expedition |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Kumaon Garhwal"/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Experts |first1=Disha |title=Indian History & Culture Quick Revision Material for UPSC & State PSC General Studies Exams |date=1 August 2021 |publisher=Disha Publications |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Indian_History_Culture_Quick_Revision_Ma/w-E9EAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&pg=PA64&printsec=frontcover |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==

Sultan [[Muhammad bin Tughluq]] launched the Qarachil Expedition to stabilize the northern borders of the Delhi Sultanate and suppress rebellions in the region<ref name="disha publication"/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Pandey |first1=Manohar |title=General Knowledge 2022 |date=8 April 2021 |publisher=Arihant Publications India limited |isbn=978-93-252-9558-2 |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/General_Knowledge_2022/sNBSEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&pg=PT79&printsec=frontcover |language=en}}</ref>. The area, identified with parts of modern-day [[Kumaon Kingdom|Kumaon]]  and [[Garhwal division|Garhwal]]<ref name="garhkumaon">{{cite book |last1=Majumdar |first1=Ramesh Chandra |title=The History and Culture of the Indian People: The Delhi sultanate |date=1951 |publisher=G. Allen & Unwin |pages=73,506 |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/The_History_and_Culture_of_the_Indian_Pe/fg1uAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&dq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&printsec=frontcover |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Kumaon Garhwal">{{cite book |last1=Pickthall |first1=Marmaduke William |last2=Asad |first2=Muhammad |title=Islamic Culture |date=1988 |publisher=Islamic Culture Board |pages=15 |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Islamic_Culture/MYJCAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&dq=qarachil+expedition+kumaon&printsec=frontcover |ref=Qarachil refer as Kumaon and the expedition done in kumaon-Garhwal hills |language=en}}</ref> in Uttarakhand, was strategically significant due to its rugged terrain and its position as a frontier zone.<ref name="kumaon"/><ref name="journal"/>

=== The campaign ===

The expedition, led by Khusrau Malik, was one of the largest undertaken by the Delhi Sultanate, with an estimated strength of 80,000 to 100,000 troops. Initially, the army advanced successfully through Sambhal and captured key territories, including Jidya. However, the campaign soon turned disastrous:
* Fierce resistance by Kumaoni forces: The local rulers and their troops employed guerrilla tactics, ambushing the sultanate's forces in the dense forests and rugged mountains. The Himalayan warriors, well-acquainted with the terrain, inflicted heavy casualties on the invaders.<ref name="kumaon"/><ref name="journal"/>
* Strategic disruption: Kumaoni forces targeted supply lines and logistical routes, starving the sultanate’s army of essential resources.<ref name="kumaon"/><ref name="journal"/>
* Adverse weather and plague: Heavy rains and freezing conditions in the mountains compounded the difficulties. The harsh climate caused widespread illness, including an outbreak of plague that devastated the sultanate’s troops.<ref name="kumaon"/><ref name="journal"/>
* Logistical failures: The sultanate forces were unprepared for the extended campaign in such remote terrain. Their reliance on traditional supply lines proved to be a significant vulnerability.<ref name="kumaon"/><ref name="journal"/>

== Aftermath ==

The failure of the Qarachil Expedition had far-reaching consequences:
* Military losses: A significant portion of the sultanate’s forces were lost, weakening its military.<ref name="kumaon"/>
* Economic strain: The expedition’s cost exacerbated financial pressures on the empire.<ref name="kumaon"/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Saeed |first1=Mian Muhammad |title=The Sharqi of Jaunpur: A Political & Cultural History |date=1972 |publisher=University of Karachi |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/The_Sharqi_of_Jaunpur/-RIdAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=0&bsq=qarachil%20expedition |language=en}}</ref>
* Forced currency: After expedition Tuglaq launched brass and copper currency <ref>{{cite book |last1=Majumdar |first1=Ramesh Chandra |last2=Raychaudhuri |first2=Hemchandra |last3=Datta |first3=Kalikinkar |title=An Advanced History of India: The Delhi sultanate and the Mughul empire |date=1949 |publisher=Macmillan and Company, Limited |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/An_Advanced_History_of_India_The_Delhi_s/TP7HAAAAIAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=0&bsq=qarachil%20expedition |language=en}}</ref>
* Political repercussions: Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq’s credibility was damaged, and dissent grew within his administration.<ref name="kumaon"/>

The Qarachil Expedition, also known as the Kumaon Expedition, was a military campaign undertaken by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq of the Delhi Sultanate during the 14th century at 1337-38CE. The campaign aimed to secure the northern frontiers.
Qarachil is also referred to as Kumaon.
